title: Vowel Harmony (Front vs. Back Vowels)
subtitle: Match suffixes to the musical character of root vowels
keyPoint: Hungarian suffixes adapt their vowels to match whether the stem contains back vowels or front vowels.

cells: a, á, o, ó, u, ú

mistakes.note: 'ház' contains the back vowel 'á', requiring the back suffix variant '-ban'.
'kert' contains the front vowel 'e', requiring the front suffix variant '-ben'.
Compound or polysyllabic back-vowel roots require back-harmonic suffixes.

quiz.question: Choose the correct suffix: 'A lány az autó___ ül.' (in the car)
quiz.explanation: 'Autó' contains the back vowels 'a' and 'ó', so it takes the back suffix '-ban'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct suffix: 'Egy szép kép van az étterem___.' (in the restaurant)
quiz.explanation: 'Étterem' has front vowels (é, e), which requires the front suffix '-ben'.

quiz.question: Which word takes the suffix variant '-hoz' (towards)?
quiz.explanation: 'Orvos' contains back vowels ('o'), taking the back suffix '-hoz'.

quiz.question: Which form correctly pairs 'erdő' (forest) with '-ben/-ban'?
quiz.explanation: 'Erdő' has front vowels (e, ő), so it takes the front variant '-ben'.

tip: When a word contains neutral vowels like 'i' or 'é' mixed with back vowels (e.g., 'kocsi', 'tányér'), the back vowel always wins!

title: Definite vs. Indefinite Conjugation
subtitle: Select your verb ending based on how specific the object is
keyPoint: Use the definite conjugation when referring to a specific, identifiable direct object, and the indefinite conjugation when the object is general, indefinite, or absent.

examples.en: Minden nap olvasom ezt a hírlapot.

mistakes.note: 'A könyvet' has a definite article 'a', so the verb must use the definite conjugation ('olvasom').
'Egy kutyát' is indefinite, so the verb must take the indefinite ending ('látok').
Demonstrative pronouns like 'ezt' (this) make the object definite.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Én ___ a levelet.' (I am writing the letter)
quiz.explanation: 'A levelet' is definite ('the letter'), so 1st person singular requires definite 'írom'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Péter ___ egy almát.' (Péter eats an apple)
quiz.explanation: 'Egy almát' is indefinite, so 3rd person singular indefinite 'eszik' is required.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Nem ___ ezt a szót.' (We don't understand this word)
quiz.explanation: 'Ezt a szót' is definite, so 1st person plural takes definite 'értjük'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Mit ___ ott a földön?' (What do you [informal] see on the ground?)
quiz.explanation: The question word 'mit' (what) triggers the indefinite conjugation ('látsz').

tip: Whenever you see 'a/az' (the), 'ez/az' (this/that), or a person's name as an object, immediately switch to the definite conjugation!

title: The Accusative Case (-t)
subtitle: Mark the direct receiver of an action with -t
keyPoint: Direct objects in Hungarian must take the accusative suffix -t, frequently preceded by a linking vowel after consonants.

useCases.label: Food and drink orders
useCases.example: Egy teát és egy szendvicset kérek.

examples.en: A fiú egy könyvet olvas csendben.

mistakes.note: Direct objects of verbs like 'kér' (to request/order) require the accusative '-t'.
Final 'a' becomes long 'á' before adding the accusative suffix '-t'.
'Ház' is the direct object and requires the linking vowel 'a' plus '-t'.

quiz.question: Form the accusative: 'Kérek egy pohár ___.' (water / víz)
quiz.explanation: 'Víz' shortens its stem vowel to 'i' and takes the linking vowel 'e', yielding 'vizet'.

quiz.question: Form the accusative: 'Szeretem ezt a ___.' (car / autó)
quiz.explanation: Words ending in long vowels like 'ó' add '-t' directly without a linking vowel: 'autót'.

quiz.question: Form the accusative: 'Veszünk egy új ___.' (table / asztal)
quiz.explanation: After 'l', the accusative '-t' can attach directly: 'asztalt'.

quiz.question: Form the accusative: 'Eszem egy piros ___.' (apple / alma)
quiz.explanation: Final 'a' lengthens to 'á' before suffixes: 'almát'.

tip: Final short vowels '-a' and '-e' ALWAYS lengthen to '-á-' and '-é-' whenever any suffix (like '-t') is added.

title: The 3x3 Spatial Case System
subtitle: Navigate interior, surface, and proximity spaces with 9 suffixes
keyPoint: Hungarian specifies spatial location across three dimensions (inside, surface, near) and three directions (moving towards, resting at, moving away).

useCases.label: Interior movement & rest
useCases.example: Bemegy a házba, és a szobában marad.

useCases.label: Visiting people / locations
useCases.example: Az orvoshoz megyek, most az orvosnál vagyok.

mistakes.note: Movement into a place requires '-ba' (into), not static '-ban' (inside).
Being statically at a person's office/place requires '-nál/-nél', not directional '-hoz'.
Static location on a surface requires the locative suffix '-on/-en/-ön/-n', not '-ra'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Gábor bemegy az iroda___.' (into the office)
quiz.explanation: Movement towards an interior space uses the illative suffix '-ba'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'A tányér az asztal___ hever.' (on the table)
quiz.explanation: Static rest on a horizontal surface requires the superessive suffix '-on'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Péter most jön a posta___.' (out from the post office)
quiz.explanation: Movement out from a building or institutional space uses '-ból' (or '-ról' if treated as surface, but '-ból' for inside).

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Ma este a barátom___ megyek vendégségbe.' (to my friend's place)
quiz.explanation: Motion toward a person uses the allative suffix '-hoz/-hez/-höz'.

tip: Remember the 3 questions: 'Hova?' (Where to?), 'Hol?' (Where at?), and 'Honnan?' (Where from?). Every spatial suffix answers exactly one of these.

title: Singular Possession of Nouns
subtitle: Indicate ownership by attaching endings directly to nouns
keyPoint: Hungarian shows ownership by suffixing the noun itself (-m for my, -d for your, -a/-e for his/her/its) rather than relying on separate possessive words.

useCases.label: Personal belongings
useCases.example: Hol van a táskád és a telefonod?

useCases.label: Parts of the body
useCases.example: Fáj a fejem és a torkom.

mistakes.note: Hungarian requires the possessive suffix on the noun ('házam'), not just the personal pronoun.
Even when using 'te' for emphasis, the noun must carry the 2nd person ending '-ed'.
Remember that both possessor and possessed can take suffixes in longer chains.

quiz.question: How do you say 'my apartment' (lakás)?
quiz.explanation: 'Lakás' is a back-vowel consonant stem, taking '-om' in 1st person singular: 'lakásom'.

quiz.question: How do you say 'your (informal) name' (név)?
quiz.explanation: 'Név' changes slightly to 'nev-' and takes the 2nd person singular suffix '-ed': 'neved'.

quiz.question: How do you say 'his/her dog' (kutya)?
quiz.explanation: Final 'a' lengthens to 'á' and adds the 3rd person suffix '-ja': 'kutyája'.

quiz.question: Which sentence means 'My head hurts'?
quiz.explanation: 1st person singular 'my head' takes '-em': 'fejem'.

tip: The personal pronouns (én, te, ő) are completely optional and only used for strong emphasis—'a táskám' is completely sufficient for 'my bag'!

title: Zero Copula in the 3rd Person Present
subtitle: Dropping 'van' and 'vannak' when describing identity or qualities
keyPoint: In the present tense, third-person singular and plural statements completely omit the verb 'to be' when linking a subject to an adjective or noun.

mistakes.note: Never use 'van' to link a 3rd person subject to a noun or adjective in the present affirmative.
'Vannak' is omitted in 3rd person plural descriptions; the adjective itself takes plural -k.
Do not drop 'van' when indicating physical location; zero copula applies only to descriptive/predicative identities.

quiz.question: How do you say 'The soup is hot'?
quiz.explanation: Third person singular drops the verb 'to be' entirely when using an adjective.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'They are students.' -> 'Ők ___.'
quiz.explanation: In 3rd person plural descriptive statements, drop 'vannak' and pluralize the noun to 'diákok'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly retains the copula because it specifies location?
quiz.explanation: Zero copula does not apply to locational expressions; 'van' must be stated for being in a place.

quiz.question: Translate: 'Erika is very kind.'
quiz.explanation: No copula is used in 3rd person present descriptive sentences, so 'Erika nagyon kedves' is correct.

tip: Remember: if you can answer 'What is it like?' or 'What is their job?', drop 'van'. If you answer 'Where is it?', keep 'van'!

title: Ik-Verbs Conjugation
subtitle: Handling the distinct singular forms of Hungarian -ik ending verbs
keyPoint: Verbs with citation forms ending in -ik take -m (instead of -k) in the 1st person singular present indefinite and display -ik in the 3rd person singular.

cells: Retains dictionary suffix -ik in indefinite form
Plural forms conjugate identically to regular verbs

examples.en: A kislány békésen alszik az ágyban.
Sajnos nem emlékszem erre a címre.

mistakes.note: While heard colloquially, standard Hungarian grammar strictly requires -m for the 1st person singular of -ik verbs.
In 3rd person singular indefinite, -ik verbs must retain the -ik ending; do not drop it like regular zero-ending verbs.
The '-ik' characteristic only affects singular conjugations; plural forms follow normal verb patterns.

quiz.question: Choose the standard form: 'I am drinking water.' -> 'Én vizet ___.'
quiz.explanation: In standard grammar, 1st person singular of 'iszik' takes the ik-suffix -om: 'iszom'.

quiz.question: How do you conjugate 'dolgozik' (to work) for 'ő' (he/she) in the indefinite present?
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person singular indefinite form of an -ik verb retains the suffix -ik.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Do you (te) eat bread?' -> '___ kenyeret?'
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person singular familiar form of 'eszik' is 'eszel'.

quiz.question: Which of the following is NOT an -ik verb?
quiz.explanation: 'Olvas' is a regular verb without an -ik dictionary ending.

tip: Think of the 'm' in 'én' matching the 'm' in 'iszom', 'alszom', and 'eszem' to easily remember the 1st person ik-ending!

title: Verbal Prefixes (Igékötők) and Detachment
subtitle: Changing aspect and shifting prefixes with negation, focus, and modals
keyPoint: Verbal prefixes attach before the verb in neutral statements, but detach and move after the verb under negation, strong focus, or when preceding an auxiliary modal verb.

cells: I am not writing the letter.
Prefix precedes modal OR follows infinitive
I want to write the letter.
It is the letter that I am writing.

useCases.label: Negated action
useCases.example: Anna ma nem megy el a moziba.

examples.en: A diákok már megcsinálták a házi feladatot.
Nem hívom fel Tamást késő este.
Most le kell ülnöm egy percre.

mistakes.note: The negator 'nem' attracts the verb directly to itself, forcing the prefix to jump behind the verb.
In standard modal constructions, the prefix detaches from the infinitive and moves in front of the conjugated modal verb.
In simple neutral affirmative statements, the verbal prefix and verb must be written as one solid word.

quiz.question: How do you negate: 'Gábor elment tegnap.'?
quiz.explanation: In negation, 'nem' precedes the verb and the prefix follows it: 'nem ment el'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly places the prefix with the modal verb 'akar' (to want)?
options: Meg akarom nézni ezt a filmet.
Akarom nézni meg ezt a filmet.
Nézni akarom meg ezt a filmet.
quiz.explanation: The prefix 'meg' detaches from 'nézni' and attaches directly in front of the modal verb 'akarom'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct neutral affirmative sentence:
quiz.explanation: In neutral word order without special focus or negation, the prefix attaches directly to the front of the verb: 'felhív'.

quiz.question: Translate: 'We must start now.' (elindulni / kell)
quiz.explanation: The verbal prefix 'el' detaches and precedes the impersonal modal 'kell': 'el kell indulnunk'.

tip: Think of 'nem' as a magnet: it pulls the verb immediately to itself, kicking the prefix out to the position right behind the verb!

title: Possession with 'Nekem van' (Dative + Copula)
subtitle: Expressing ownership using the dative case and the verb 'lenni'
keyPoint: Hungarian has no verb for 'to have'; instead, it expresses possession using the formula: Possessor in Dative (-nak/-nek) + 'van/vannak' + Possessed Item with a possessive suffix.

cells: I have a car (To me there is a car)
I don't have time (There is no time to me)

mistakes.note: Hungarian does not use an active transitive 'have' verb in daily speech; use 'nekem van + possessive suffix'.
'Nem van' is ungrammatical; it always fuses into 'nincs' (or 'nincsenek' for plural items).
The named owner must take the dative suffix -nak/-nek.

quiz.question: How do you say 'I have a dog'?
quiz.explanation: The possessor takes dative 'nekem', the copula is 'van', and the possessed item takes the 1st person suffix '-m'.

quiz.question: What is the correct negative form of 'Nekik van kocsijuk' (They have a car)?
quiz.explanation: Because 'kocsijuk' is singular, 'nem van' contracts to 'nincs'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'The boy has a ticket.' -> 'A fiú___ van jegye.'
quiz.explanation: A named possessor takes the dative suffix; front-vowel/back-vowel harmony gives 'fiúnak'.

quiz.question: Translate: 'We don't have questions.' (kérdés)
quiz.explanation: When the possessed items are plural ('kérdéseink'), the plural negative existential 'nincsenek' must be used.

tip: The pronouns 'nekem', 'neked', etc., can be dropped if context is clear ('Van egy kutyám'), but named owners must always take '-nak' or '-nek'!

title: Possession of Multiple Objects (-aim, -aid, -ai)
subtitle: Attaching plural possessed suffixes to show multiple owned items
keyPoint: When the items possessed are plural, Hungarian inserts an 'i' possessive marker before the personal ending (-aim, -aid, -ai / -eim, -eid, -ei).

useCases.label: Talking about family members or friends

examples.en: A tanár válaszol a diákok kérdéseire.

mistakes.note: Do not attach the regular plural '-k' before possessive suffixes; use the specialized '-i-' plural possessive marker.
Never add '-ok/-ek' after a possessive suffix. 'My friends' is 'barátaim', not 'barátomok'.
Do not stack double plurals; '-aim' already denotes both plurality of the keys and the 1st person owner.

quiz.question: How do you say 'my books' (singular: könyv)?
quiz.explanation: 'Könyv' takes front-vowel plural possessive endings: 'könyveim'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for 'his/her friends' (singular: barát):
quiz.explanation: 'Barát' takes the 3rd person singular possessor + plural possessed suffix '-jai'.

quiz.question: Complete the question: 'Where are your (singular informal) keys?' -> 'Hol vannak a kulcs___?'
quiz.explanation: 'Kulcs' is a back-vowel noun, so 'your keys' becomes 'kulcsaid'.

quiz.question: What is the meaning of 'a gyerekeink'?
quiz.explanation: The suffix '-eink' indicates 1st person plural possessor ('our') and plural possessed items ('children').

tip: Spot the letter 'i'! Whenever you possess MORE THAN ONE thing, an 'i' will always appear in the possessive suffix (e.g., kutyá-m = 1 dog, kutyá-i-m = 2+ dogs).

title: Inflected Postpositions and Case Pronouns
subtitle: Attaching possessive endings to case suffixes and spatial adverbs
keyPoint: Hungarian expresses combinations of pronouns and prepositions by adding possessive endings directly to case markers or postpositions instead of using independent words.

useCases.label: Physical spatial relationship
useCases.example: A macska mögöttem alszik a fotelben.

useCases.label: Possession or accompaniment
useCases.example: Van nálad elég pénz a vacsorára?

examples.en: A kisfiú elbújt mögöttem a parkban.
Nincs nála telefon, ezért nem érjük el.

mistakes.note: Hungarian never uses independent personal pronouns after raw case endings; the ending itself inflects.
Cases like -nál/-nél take personal possessive suffixes rather than stand-alone subject pronouns.
Postpositions decline like possessed nouns when referring to personal pronouns.

quiz.question: Can you count on me? -> Számíthatsz ___?
quiz.explanation: The verb 'számít' takes the sub引导 case (-ra/-re), which becomes 'rám' for 1st person singular.

quiz.question: Do you have the keys with you? -> Nálad vannak a kulcsok?
quiz.explanation: 'Nálad' means 'at you' or 'in your possession' (informal singular).

quiz.question: The dog is walking behind us. -> A kutya ___ sétál.
quiz.explanation: The postposition 'mögött' plus the 1st person plural ending '-ünk' yields 'mögöttünk'.

quiz.question: Peter came over to our place yesterday. -> Péter tegnap átjött ___.
quiz.explanation: 'Hozzánk' is the inflected form of the allative case for 1st person plural (to us / to our place).

tip: Think of these words as nouns that own a relationship: 'benn-em' literally behaves like 'in-my-ness', using familiar possessive endings (-m, -d, -e/-a).

title: Topic-Focus Syntax and Pre-Verbal Focus Position
subtitle: Manipulating word order to emphasize new or contrastive information
keyPoint: Hungarian word order is pragmatic rather than grammatical; the element placed immediately before the conjugated verb receives the exclusive focus and primary stress.

cells: It was AN APPLE that Peter ate (not a pear).
PETER was the one who ate an apple.
Peter DID eat an apple (asserting truth).

useCases.label: Contrastive identification
useCases.example: Anna a könyvet olvassa, nem az újságot.

useCases.label: Verbal prefix detachment
useCases.example: János nem ment el a buliba tegnap este.

examples.en: Nem én törtem el a vázát.
Csak két levelet küldtem el ma.

mistakes.note: When a focused noun occupies the pre-verbal spot, the verbal prefix (meg-) must move behind the verb.
Question words naturally occupy the focus slot, requiring the verb prefix to detach and follow the verb.
Restricting modifiers like 'csak' (only) must sit inside the pre-verbal focus position together with their noun.

quiz.question: It was AN APPLE that Anna ate (not a pear). -> Anna ___ evett meg.
quiz.explanation: Placing 'almát' directly before the verb 'evett' stresses that the apple was the specific object consumed.

quiz.question: Where does the verbal prefix 'el' go when 'Péter' is emphasized as the doer? -> PÉTER ___ tegnap.
quiz.explanation: When an element takes focus ahead of the verb, separable prefixes like 'el-' are pushed behind the verb: 'PÉTER ment el'.

quiz.question: Who called you yesterday? -> Ki ___ fel tegnap?
quiz.explanation: 'Ki' is in focus, so the preverbal prefix 'fel-' must detach to after the verb: 'Ki hívott fel?'

quiz.question: Only Mary understood the lesson. -> Csak Mária ___ meg a leckét.
quiz.explanation: 'Csak Mária' occupies the focus slot, demanding verb inversion where 'értette' precedes 'meg'.

tip: Spot the focus by locating the verb: whatever sits directly in front of the conjugated stem (and boots the verbal prefix backwards) carries the spotlight.

title: Past Tense Definite and Indefinite Forms
subtitle: Navigating the three stem classes and dual conjugation in the past
keyPoint: Past tense verbs attach -t, -tt, or a linking vowel plus -tt before taking indefinite or definite personal markers based on stem phonology and transitivity.

cells: Class 2: Stem ending in two consonants or long vowel + t

useCases.label: Indefinite past action
useCases.example: Gábor tegnap egy új autót vásárolt.

useCases.label: Past event without an object
useCases.example: A gyerekek egész délután a kertben játszottak.

examples.en: A diákok figyelmesen hallgatták a tanárt.
Láttátok a híres filmet a moziban?
Reggel korán ébredtem, és főztem egy kávét.

mistakes.note: '-ott' marks 3rd person singular indefinite; 1st person requires '-tam' or '-tem'.

mistakes.right: Láttam a filmet tegnap. / Láttam egy filmet.
mistakes.note: Remember vowel harmony and transitivity: with 'a filmet' (definite), use 'láttam' (definite 1st person matches indefinite here, but 3rd person distinguishes 'látta' vs 'látott').
When the object has a definite article ('a kép'), the definite conjugation suffix '-te' must be used instead of indefinite '-t/-ett'.

quiz.question: Yesterday they sold the car. -> Tegnap ___ az autót.
quiz.explanation: 'Az autót' is definite, and the subject is 'they' (3rd person plural), requiring definite '-ták': 'eladták'.

quiz.question: I waited for a bus for an hour. -> Egy órát ___ a buszra.
quiz.explanation: The 1st person singular past indefinite form of 'várni' is 'vártam'.

quiz.question: What did you (informal singular) drink? -> Mit ___ tegnap?
quiz.explanation: The past indefinite 2nd person singular of the irregular stem 'iszik' is 'ittál'.

quiz.question: The boy opened the door. -> A fiú ___ az ajtót.
quiz.explanation: 'Az ajtót' is a definite object; 3rd person singular past definite takes '-otta': 'kinyitotta'.

tip: In 3rd person singular, bare '-t' only appears after sonorant consonants (-l, -r, -n, -ny, -j) or sibilants; clusters of two consonants always demand a linking vowel + '-tt'.

title: The First-to-Second Person Suffix (-lak/-lek)
subtitle: Connecting 1st person singular subjects to 2nd person objects
keyPoint: Whenever the grammatical subject is 'I' (én) and the direct object is 'you' (téged, titeket, or benneteket), Hungarian contracts the relationship into the dedicated verbal suffix -lak or -lek.

examples.en: Sajnos tegnap este nem láttalak a színházban.

mistakes.note: Using the standard definite 1st person suffix (-m) with a 2nd person pronoun object is ungrammatical; -lak/-lek is required.
'-lak/-lek' is strictly for a 1st person singular ('én') subject acting on a 2nd person object; plural 'mi' uses normal plural endings.
While pronoun inclusion adds emphasis, adding redundant 'téged' before polite requests like 'kérlek szépen' sounds unnatural.

quiz.question: I hear you very well. -> Nagyon jól ___ téged.
quiz.explanation: Subject 'én' + object 'téged' combines with back-vowel stem 'hall-' into 'hallak'.

quiz.question: I will invite you (plural) to dinner. -> ___ titeket vacsorára.
quiz.explanation: The suffix '-lak/-lek' covers both singular 'you' and plural 'you (titeket)' objects when 'I' perform the action.

quiz.question: I waited for you for two hours yesterday. -> Tegnap két órát ___ az állomáson.
quiz.explanation: In past tense, the past marker '-t(a)-' is inserted before '-lak', producing 'vártalak'.

quiz.question: Please close the door! -> ___, zárd be az ajtót!
quiz.explanation: 'Kérlek' (I ask you) is the standard polite formula derived from 'kér' + '-lek'.

tip: Remember: -lak/-lek is exclusively one-directional: from ME to YOU. It cannot be used if 'we' (mi) do the action, even if the target is 'you'.

title: Conditional Mood (Present and Past)
subtitle: Expressing hypothetical, polite, and counterfactual events
keyPoint: The present conditional is built with the -na/-ne/-ná/-né mood markers before personal endings, while the past conditional pairs past tense verbs with the auxiliary particle 'volna'.

cells: I would learn / I would ask
He would learn it / ask it
I would see you / ask you
I would have gone / he would have seen it

useCases.label: Hypothetical condition (Present)
useCases.example: Ha lenne elég időm, többet olvasnék.

useCases.label: Counterfactual past regret
useCases.example: Ha tudtam volna, elmentem volna a találkozóra.

examples.en: Mit csinálnál, ha nyernél a lottón?
Ha nem esett volna az eső, kirándultunk volna.
Megvenném ezt a kabátot, de túl drága.

mistakes.right: Ha tudtam volna tegnap, segítettem volna.
mistakes.note: For unfulfilled conditions in the past, use the past indicative verb + 'volna', never the present conditional.
In 1st person singular present conditional, indefinite uses '-nék' for all vowel harmonies; '-nám/-ném' is definite.

mistakes.wrong: Ha én lennék gazdag, vennék volna egy házat.
mistakes.right: Ha én gazdag lennék, vennék egy házat.
mistakes.note: Do not mix past conditional marker 'volna' into a purely present hypothetical wish.

quiz.question: I would like to order a coffee. -> ___ kérni egy kávét.
quiz.explanation: 'Szeretnék' is the 1st person singular present conditional indefinite form used for polite requests.

quiz.question: If you had told me, I would have helped. -> Ha szóltál volna, ___ volna.
quiz.explanation: Past conditional requires a past tense verb paired with 'volna': 'segítettem volna'.

quiz.question: What would you (singular) do in my place? -> Te mit ___ a helyemben?
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person singular present conditional indefinite of 'csinál' is 'csinálnál'.

quiz.question: If we had enough money, we would buy the flat. -> Ha lenne pénzünk, ___ a lakást.
quiz.explanation: 'A lakást' is a definite object; the 1st person plural present conditional definite suffix is '-nénk': 'megvennénk'.

tip: Notice that unlike most tenses, 1st person singular indefinite conditional always ends in '-nék' regardless of whether the verb stem contains back or front vowels (e.g., várnék and kérnék).

title: Subjunctive-Imperative Mood (Felszólító mód)
subtitle: Forming direct orders, requests, and subordinate wish clauses
keyPoint: The subjunctive-imperative is formed using the marker -j-, which often assimilates thoroughly into preceding sibilant and dental stem consonants.

useCases.label: Subordinate Clauses (hogy)
useCases.example: Azt akarom, hogy gyere el velünk.

examples.en: Kérlek, nyisd ki a könyvet a huszadik oldalon!
Fontos, hogy mindennap olvass egy keveset.
Ne fuss olyan gyorsan, mert elesel!
A tanár azt kéri, hogy figyeljünk az órán.
Segíts a nagymamának cipelni a csomagot!

mistakes.note: Subordinate clauses expressing wishes or requests after 'hogy' require the subjunctive form, not the indicative.
The suffix -j assimilates completely to sibilants like 's', becoming -ss- instead of retaining 'sj'.
Verb stems ending in long vowel + t take -s- rather than -j- in the imperative mood.

quiz.question: Choose the correct imperative form: '___ be a könyvet!' (Close the book! - definite, te)
quiz.explanation: For a definite object with 'te', 'csuk' takes the definite imperative ending -d, forming 'csukd'.

quiz.question: Complete the clause: 'Azt akarom, hogy Péter ___ ide.' (I want Peter to come here.)
quiz.explanation: Third-person singular subjunctive of the irregular verb 'jön' is 'jöjjön'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct command: '___ egy kicsit lassabban!' (Drive a bit slower! - te)
quiz.explanation: The stem 'vezet' ends in short vowel + t, which mutates to -ss- in the imperative: 'vezess'.

quiz.question: Let's go home together! -> '___ haza együtt!'
quiz.explanation: 'Menjünk' is the first-person plural (mi) subjunctive form used for 'let us'.

tip: Remember that whenever a main clause expresses intention, request, or necessity with 'hogy' (e.g., 'kell, hogy...', 'akarom, hogy...'), the verb in the subclause must always be subjunctive.

title: Causative and Reflexive Derivation
subtitle: Deriving actions done to oneself or caused to be done by others
keyPoint: Causative suffixes (-at/-et/-tat/-tet) make someone do an action, while reflexive endings (-kodik/-kedik/-ködik or -kozik/-kezik/-közik) reflect the action onto the subject.

useCases.label: Services & Delegated Work
useCases.example: Holnap megjavíttatom a telefonomat a szervizben.

useCases.label: Personal Hygiene & Care
useCases.example: Reggelente gyorsan megfésülködöm a tükör előtt.

useCases.label: Active Behavior
useCases.example: A gyerekek nagyon udvariasan viselkednek az iskolában.

examples.en: A mesterrel festetem ki a nappalit a jövő héten.
Péter minden reggel tíz perc alatt felöltözködik.
Nem szeretem megváratni a vendégeket az étteremben.
A fiú hosszan törülközik az edzés után.
Az orvos felíratja a szükséges gyógyszereket.

mistakes.note: If someone else washes it for you at a facility, use the causative 'mosat' instead of plain 'mos'.
Without the reflexive suffix, 'borotválom' requires an external object because it means 'I shave (someone/something)'.
The monosyllabic verb 'ír' takes -at, yielding 'írat', not the double-t suffix 'írtat'.

quiz.question: I have my hair cut at the barber. -> '___ a hajamat a fodrásszal.'
quiz.explanation: 'Levágat' is the causative form of 'levág', showing that the barber is hired to cut your hair.

quiz.question: Anna gets dressed quickly every morning. -> 'Anna minden reggel gyorsan ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'Öltözködik' is the reflexive form meaning 'to dress oneself'.

quiz.question: The teacher makes the students write a test. -> 'A tanár dolgozatot ___ a diákokkal.'
quiz.explanation: 'Írat' is the causative form of 'ír', meaning 'to make/have someone write'.

quiz.question: Choose the reflexive verb for 'to introduce oneself':
quiz.explanation: 'Bemutatkozik' means to introduce oneself, formed with the reflexive suffix -kozik.

tip: When identifying the person performing the delegated causative task, Hungarian almost always puts that agent in the instrumental case (-val/-vel): 'Péterrel csináltatom meg' (I'll have Peter do it).

title: The Potential Verb Form (-hat/-het)
subtitle: Expressing permission and possibility inside the verb stem
keyPoint: The productive suffix -hat/-het attaches immediately after the verb root to indicate possibility or permission ('may' or 'can').

cells: could / would be able to go

useCases.label: Speculation & Likelihood
useCases.example: Késő van, már alhatnak a szomszédok.

examples.en: Szabad itt dohányozni, vagy csak kint dohányozhatunk?
Holnap sajnos nem jöhetek a születésnapi bulidra.
Ezt a feladatot könnyen megcsinálhatjátok együtt.
Már indulhatunk, mindenki elkészült a pakolással.

mistakes.note: 'Tud' denotes learned skill or internal capacity; for permission or circumstantial ability, use the -hat/-het suffix.

mistakes.wrong: Nem láthatlak téged. (meaning sight is blocked)
mistakes.note: 'Nem láthatlak' implies a ban or external prohibition; if you simply cannot see someone, use plain 'látlak'.
Never add -hat/-het directly to an infinitive ending in -ni; it forms an independent conjugable finite verb.

quiz.question: Excuse me, may I ask a question? -> 'Elnézést, ___ egy kérdést?'
quiz.explanation: 'Kérdez' takes back vowel -hat; with indefinite 1st person singular ending -ek, it becomes 'kérdezhetek'.

quiz.question: You can leave your coat here. (te, definite) -> 'Itt ___ a kabátodat.'
quiz.explanation: Definite direct object ('a kabátodat') with subject 'te' requires the definite suffix: 'hagyhatod'.

quiz.question: Could we sit down here? -> '___ ide?'
quiz.explanation: 'Leülhetnénk' combines both potential (-het-) and polite conditional (-nénk) moods.

quiz.question: He could not sleep last night. -> 'Tegnap este nem ___.'
quiz.explanation: Past potential combines stem 'al-' + -hat- + past tense marker -ott: 'alhatott'.

tip: You can stack moods! The potential marker -hat/-het always precedes tense and conditional markers (e.g., vár + hat + na = várhatna 'he could wait').

title: Adverbial Participles (-va/-ve, -ván/-vén)
subtitle: Modifying clauses to express manner, cause, or accompanying state
keyPoint: Adverbial participles end in -va/-ve (or archaic -ván/-vén) and describe the state of the subject or manner in which an action unfolds.

useCases.label: Simultaneous Manner
useCases.example: Sírdogálva mesélte el a szomorú történetet.

useCases.label: Resulting State with 'van'
useCases.example: Az ablak szélesre van nyitva egész nap.

useCases.label: Cause / Circumstance (-ván/-vén)
useCases.example: Látván a nehéz helyzetet, azonnal segített.

examples.en: A nagypapa a fotelben ülve olvasta az újságot.
Minden számla pontosan ki van fizetve.
Futva érkezett meg a vasútállomásra, nehogy lekésse a vonatot.
Ismerve a szokásait, biztosan késni fog negyedórát.
Az ajtó zárva volt, ezért csengetnünk kellett.

mistakes.note: Hungarian avoids passive constructions with '-va van' when an active agent is present. Use the active voice instead.
Dynamic or simple actions use finite past tense; do not use 'ülve voltam' to mimic English continuous tenses.

mistakes.wrong: Futva a fiú látta a kutyát.
mistakes.right: A fiú futva látta meg a kutyát.
mistakes.note: Word order matters: keep the adverbial participle close to the verb it modifies for natural flow.

quiz.question: She listened to the concert with eyes closed. -> 'Csukott szemmel, csendben ___ hallgatta a koncertet.'
quiz.explanation: 'Ülve' is the standard modern adverbial participle expressing the manner/state during the action.

quiz.question: The store is closed today. -> 'A bolt ma zárva ___.'
quiz.explanation: The stative construction describing a state uses the adverbial participle + 'van': 'zárva van'.

quiz.question: Knowing the truth, he decided not to speak. (literary) -> 'A valóságot ___, úgy döntött, nem szól semmit.'
quiz.explanation: The literary/archaic form expressing circumstance/cause is '-ván/-vén': 'tudván'.

quiz.question: They walked home singing. -> '___ sétáltak hazafelé az utcán.'
quiz.explanation: 'Énekelve' describes the accompanying simultaneous action (singing).

tip: Use '-va/-ve van' strictly to express the resulting state of an object (e.g. 'meg van írva' = it is in a written state), never to translate English continuous forms like 'I am writing'.

title: Adjectival Participles (-ó/-ő, -t/-tt, -andó/-endő)
subtitle: Compressing relative clauses into present, past, and future participles
keyPoint: Hungarian compresses relative clauses into prenominal participles: active present (-ó/-ő), completed past (-t/-tt), and mandatory future (-andó/-endő).

useCases.label: Simultaneous Action Modifier
useCases.example: A padon alvó macska nagyon aranyos.

useCases.label: Completed State Modifier
useCases.example: Az elrontott számítógépet a szervizbe vitték.

useCases.label: Obligation / Future Task
useCases.example: A megoldandó feladatok listája igen hosszú.

examples.en: A sarokban beszélgető diákok nem figyeltek a tanárra.
Gondosan elolvasta a tegnap kapott levelet.
A jövő héten elvégzendő munkát előre megterveztük.
A gyorsan múló idő mindenkit emlékeztet a céljaira.
A pincér letette az asztalra a megrendelt ételeket.

mistakes.wrong: A fiú aki olvas könyvet ott ül.
mistakes.right: A könyvet olvasó fiú ott ül.
mistakes.note: While relative clauses with 'aki' exist, native Hungarian strongly prefers compressing them into pre-nominal participial phrases.

mistakes.wrong: A fizetendő számla fizetve kell lennie.
mistakes.note: The -andó/-endő participle already carries the meaning of necessity ('must be done'); do not combine it pleonastically with modal verbs.

mistakes.wrong: A megfőzött anya finom levest adott.
mistakes.right: A megfőzött leves nagyon finom volt.
mistakes.note: Transitive past participles modify the object receiving the action (the soup), never the agent (mother) who cooked it.

quiz.question: The girl singing on the stage is my sister. -> 'A színpadon ___ lány a testvérem.'
quiz.explanation: The present active participle ending for 'énekel' is -ő, producing 'éneklő'.

quiz.question: I cannot find the purchased ticket. -> 'Nem találom a már ___ jegyet.'
quiz.explanation: 'Megvásárolt' is the past participle describing a completed action done to the ticket.

quiz.question: Tasks to be completed today must be submitted by 5 PM. -> 'A ma ___ feladatokat ötig le kell adni.'
quiz.explanation: -andó expresses future obligation or actions that need to be carried out ('to be solved').

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase: 'the decaying fallen leaves'
quiz.explanation: 'Lehullott' is the past participle of the intransitive verb 'lehull' (fallen).

tip: In Hungarian, participial phrases always precede the noun they modify, along with all their internal objects and adverbs (e.g., 'a tegnap este Budapesten vásárolt könyv' = the book bought yesterday evening in Budapest).
